sources.citation: RWAAI / Lund Humanities Lab Archive: Semaq Beri > Kruspe Collection > HGLC ('Linguistic and ethnographic documentation of hunter-gatherer languages in contact: Semoq Beri and Batek'; sites Berua and Pergam; sub-nodes Grammar, Lexicon, Field recordings, Ethnography, Images). hdl:10050/00-0000-0000-0003-66DE-7
sources.note: Only collection metadata visible; the 'Grammar' node is a 2 KiB CMDI record ('Grammatical key') with no readable document; files require an archive login.

sources.citation: Kruspe, Nicole & Asifa Majid. 2022/2023. The linguistics of odour in Semaq Beri and Semelai, two Austroasiatic languages of the Malay Peninsula. Studies in Language 47(3): 599-642. doi:10.1075/sl.22004.kru (CC BY 4.0).
sources.note: Full text grepped: silent on stress/accent/prosody. Footnote 3 (p. 602) gives only orthographic conventions (/ɟ/=j, /j/=y, /ɕ/=s, /ɑ/ written ɒ).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid record sema1265 (MEDs: Kruspe 2015 grammar_sketch 44 pp.; Karim & Ibrahim 1979 wordlist 15 pp.; Skeat & Blagden 1906 wordlist) and Grambank sema1265 (coder T. Weber, sole source Kruspe 2015).
sources.note: Nothing on stress; confirm Kruspe 2015 is the only descriptive source for the language.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Semaq Beri language' (rev. 1373073884), section Phonology > Word structure, paraphrasing Kruspe 2014: 475-480.
sources.note: No prose statement about stress. Relays Kruspe's word template with a stress mark on the final syllable: 'The typical phonological template of Semaq Beri ranges from [CV] to [Cə.'CVC].' (footnote to Kruspe 2014: 477). Tertiary relay; not catalog-grade.

sources.citation: Malaysian repository searches (USM, UiTM, UM studentsrepo, UniSZA, UKM ptsldigital) and Crossref/archive.org/Persée/LUP searches for 'Semaq Beri' / 'Semoq Beri'.
sources.note: No phonology or grammar thesis exists in these repositories; hits are ethnographic/socio-economic (Ramle Abdullah, Kimball Morris, Majid & Kruspe 2018 Current Biology).

sources.note: Not opened. Brill DOI returns a JavaScript CAPTCHA to automated fetch and 403 to web lookups; no open copy on Lund LUP (record 5153900 has no file), RWAAI, Google Books (blocked). Per Wikipedia's page citations, the phonology (word structure, phonemes) is on pp. 477-480; the only description of the language.
